cells.tense: The adjustment is being made right now, and the whole holds because of it.
cells.act: keep the ritual and give it room to change
cells.ask: Take a meal or a call you share with people — some repeated thing — and alter one part of it on purpose, out where they can see, and stay while it settles.
cells.core:
You can be inside something and see it whole at the same time. You feel where the talk is heading, what the moment needs, when to push and when to leave it alone, and you make the adjustment without stepping out. That isn't watching from the edge. It's the reading and the belonging happening in the same act.

What you read tends to stay in your hands, though, and a shape nobody else can move gets old around you. Take some repeated thing you share and alter one part of it where they can see — a call on a different day, a seat moved at the table, an old date marked a new way. Stay while that settles. Then the ones inside it can learn it from you instead of only receiving it, and it keeps breathing.
cells.sheetLine: You feel the whole room and stay in it.
cells.verb: attuning, continuously sensing when to add and when to hold back
cells.place: seeing the whole pattern from inside it

cells.tense: The smoothing will keep arriving ahead of the moment that needs it.
cells.ask: Put the want you've been holding back from someone out tonight, before the ground is level, and then don't smooth the answer that comes.
cells.core:
You see the room early, so you smooth it early. The split is visible before it opens, the friction before it starts, and by the time anyone else feels the bump it has been blended away. From outside it looks like steadiness. From inside, the adjusting rarely pauses, and whatever you want has to wait for a level moment, and the level moment keeps not coming.

Some of that smoothing is real skill and worth keeping. Some is work done before it was asked for. Put the want you've been holding back out while things are still uneven — no arranging first, no cushion — and resist the pull to manage what comes back. One honest, unfinished thing in the open won't break the room. It gives the balance something true to hold.

cells.tense: Each engagement has been pulling you apart, and a center has stayed out of reach.
cells.act: sit with someone in it without fixing it
cells.ask: Sit with one person while they're going through something hard and take in what they carry — no fixing, no advice — keeping your own footing while you stay.
cells.core:
You walk in beside people and come away in pieces. A conversation pulls you one way, a mood takes some of you with it, and nothing holds long enough to read anything whole. What you can see is everything, all at once, from everywhere — and the one place to read it from has gone missing.

Contact reaches that from the side. Sit with one person and what they're carrying, without fixing any of it. Take it in and keep your own side while you stay. It's the smallest possible act and it does two things: somebody gets met, and you are, for that stretch, unmistakably one person in one spot. The reading comes back through the contact rather than through more watching.

cells.tense: The adjusting is running now, and none of it has been counted as yours.
cells.act: learn how the people before you did it
cells.ask: Find whoever carried this before you and ask how they learned it, listening for where they altered it to keep it alive.
cells.core:
You've been tuning something shared, small move by small move, and your account of it has you following the way it already was. It wasn't already that way. The shape it takes now in your hands exists partly because you kept adjusting it, and you describe it as something you found.

Go find out how the ones before you did it — not to copy, but to meet it as made, by people, with changes in it. Find whoever carried it before you and ask how they learned it, then listen for where they altered it to keep it alive. Almost every practice that lasts has been rewritten by whoever held it. Hearing that said out loud is how you'll know it's what you've been doing.
cells.sheetLine: You're tuning what you share and calling it following.
